when you delete your voat account (why would anyone do this?), your entire account history is deleted, we don't leave your comments, votes and posts in our database

I think this is a really bad idea. It means that 1) I can't delete my account without losing all my posts and making a hole on every discussion I participated in. This is not necessarily something I want to happen, which is bad by itself, but it also makes deleting my account difficult, which is also bad. And 2) every time an account is deleted we get a hole in every discussion that user participated in, and risk losing some potentially historical data.

1 can be solved by making the erasure of posts optional. 2 would require it to be not an option, but impossible (short of manually deleting posts).

Also, remember that between deleting posts completely and keeping them untouched, there's the option of redacting the username only.

I won't say I didn't enjoy Clerks II, but I don't think it stands up to the original. Overall It lessons the franchise. Unless you can honestly tell yourself "The sequel will be even better", you probably shouldn't make a sequel.

There are two reasons why sequels (usually) suck:

  1. It has the advantage of being able to surprise you. You don't know what to expect. It seems fresh, and new.

  2. When someone makes a movie they put out their best material. Most movie makers don't ration out their ideas for a sequel that might never happen. They put all their eggs into one basket. So, in the first movie, usually, a lot of the really creative ideas are used up.

  3. It's hard to strike a balance when making a sequel. It has to be old and new at the same time. If you stray too much in a sequel you don't fulfill people's desires to relive am experience. But at the same time if it's too much of the same, then they think it's old, and stale. So you have to find out what to stick to, what to abandon, and what to recreate.

  4. Sequels tend to be rushed. It's not like the first movie. The first movie that person took their time. They could take their time because there were no expectations. But when you make a sequel then you have people breathing down your neck, trying to push out another movie.
One thing's for certain, it'll be funnier than Tusk.
